unused_menu_senses.translation: to destroy completely, to defeat thoroughly

canonical_example.text: Ele acabou com ela.
canonical_example.translation: He broke up with her.

source_metadata.etymology_text: From Old Galician-Portuguese acabar, from Vulgar Latin *accapāre. Compare Spanish acabar, French achever and English achieve. By surface analysis, a- + cabo + -ar.
raw_glosses: (intransitive) to break up with (to end a relationship with) [with com ‘someone’]

unused_menu_senses.translation: to break up with (to end a relationship with)

canonical_example.text: No fim, acabamos comendo naquele restaurante maltrapilho.
canonical_example.translation: In the end, we ended up eating at that shabby restaurant.

source_metadata.etymology_text: From Old Galician-Portuguese acabar, from Vulgar Latin *accapāre. Compare Spanish acabar, French achever and English achieve. By surface analysis, a- + cabo + -ar.

canonical_example.text: Acabe suas tarefas antes de sair.
canonical_example.translation: Finish your chores before going out.

source_metadata.etymology_text: From Old Galician-Portuguese acabar, from Vulgar Latin *accapāre. Compare Spanish acabar, French achever and English achieve. By surface analysis, a- + cabo + -ar.

unused_menu_senses.translation: to complete; to finish (to make done)

canonical_example.text: Essa lei acabará com a impunidade.

source_metadata.etymology_text: From Old Galician-Portuguese acabar, from Vulgar Latin *accapāre. Compare Spanish acabar, French achever and English achieve. By surface analysis, a- + cabo + -ar.

canonical_example.text: Todo o dinheiro acabou.

source_metadata.etymology_text: From Old Galician-Portuguese acabar, from Vulgar Latin *accapāre. Compare Spanish acabar, French achever and English achieve. By surface analysis, a- + cabo + -ar.
